recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-36242 unless a future build/link-check run identifies a new case-sensitive extension target failure.
issue_request: FHIR-36242 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction raised against R4 for R5. It reported that case-broken links to extension pages, including the Questionnaire definitionBased extension link, were not being surfaced as build errors.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the link checker already detected these problems but logged them instead of reporting errors, and that Kindling 755c14d changed the reporting while R4B d0e0fe08b0 and R5 9825def2f5 fixed remaining bad references. Local history includes the R5 commit changing extension-questionnaire-definitionBased.html, extension-ordinalValue.html, and inventoryReport.html to correctly cased targets, and the R4B commit fixing ordinalValue.
additional_context: The current source has since moved the Questionnaire extension references from old core extension-*.html pages to the Extension Pack location macro and StructureDefinition file names. The questionnaire-definitionBased extension is present in the Extension Pack with the same mixed-case id and canonical URL, so the current [%extensions-location%]StructureDefinition-questionnaire-definitionBased.html link matches the maintained extension artifact rather than regressing to the old lowercase core extension page.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Questionnaire source currently points at the Extension Pack StructureDefinition target, the historical bad-case links named in the implementation commit are absent, and no Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that would require a different current-spec change.
